topic: Project revival as IFC/World Bank-advised gas-to-power PPP, with Egyptian gas supply (2025-2026)
wiki_text: Lebanon's LNG-import effort has consolidated around the Deir Ammar site in the north, superseding the earlier Selaata, Zahrani and Beddawi FSRU concepts. In June 2025 the World Bank began publishing Expression-of-Interest tenders (legal, environmental & social, and technical advisors) for a 'Lebanon Gas-to-Power' project centred on an FSRU at Deir Ammar. In November 2025 the International Finance Corporation (IFC) signed an advisory agreement to act as lead transaction advisor to the Government of Lebanon, working with the High Council for Privatization and PPPs and the Ministry of Energy and Water to structure the scheme as a public-private partnership. The broader project envisions the FSRU plus modernization of the existing ~465 MW Deir Ammar I plant and a new ~825 MW combined-cycle plant (Deir Ammar II). In January 2026 Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum signed a memorandum of understanding to supply natural gas to the Deir Ammar power plant via the Arab Gas Pipeline. As of mid-2026 the project remains pre-FID and in the advisory/feasibility phase, with no developer yet selected; the Lebanese Ministry of Energy and Water remains the public sponsor.
